question: Does a primary Laguna de Bay study provide useful natural-diet evidence for Chitala ornata, and is that evidence suitable for public Bangwit reuse?

bibliography.title: Diet Variation and Prey Composition of Exotic Clown Featherback, Chitala ornata (Gray 1831) (Osteoglossiformes: Notopteridae) in Laguna De Bay, Luzon Island, Philippines
bibliography.author: Mark Nell Castillo Corpuz

studyAssessment.scope: Three lake regions described as west, central, and east. The publisher abstract does not supply exact station coordinates.
studyAssessment.samplingAndAnalysis: The abstract reports 203 Chitala ornata specimens collected using fish traps, seining, and gill nets; 12 empty stomachs were excluded, leaving 191 stomachs for prey analysis. Eleven prey items were identified.

sourceReportedDiet.sizeAndSiteVariation: The authors report that smaller fish up to 45 cm mainly consumed crustaceans, while fish over 46 cm mainly consumed teleosts. The abstract also reports higher prey diversity and teleost consumption in the central lake region. Preserve these as study-specific findings, not a universal diet rule.

studyAssessment.interpretation: This is direct stomach-content evidence for one predator species in Laguna de Bay during early 2014. The abstract names only its leading prey groups/items and does not provide the full prey list, event-level records, or exact stations. It is natural-diet evidence, not tested bait effectiveness or fishing advice.
limitations: Historical sampling from January-March 2014 does not establish the current diet of the species.
The three-region result is local to Laguna de Bay and must not be generalized to other lakes, rivers, sizes, seasons, or populations.
The publisher PDF link was visible, but the web reader returned a cache-miss error; this review used the publisher abstract only and did not inspect the full text or tables.
The source abstract's reported length thresholds leave the interval around 46 cm unstated; any later user-facing display should retain the source's wording or verify the full text first.
No prey-name taxonomic crosswalk, bait recommendation, occurrence record, geometry, or app diet row was created.

accessAndRights.abstractAccess: The article abstract and citation were reviewed on the official Asian Fisheries Society publisher page.
accessAndRights.fullTextAccess: A publisher PDF link is offered on the article and issue pages. The PDF fetch returned a cache-miss error during this review; no local PDF was downloaded or retained.
accessAndRights.journalPolicy: The current Asian Fisheries Science author guide says all AFS articles are licensed CC BY-NC 4.0. The 2018 article page does not display an item-specific license statement; application of the current journal-wide statement to this older issue was not independently confirmed.
accessAndRights.decision: Use the source only as a cited research lead until the article-level license and Bangwit's compatibility with the noncommercial condition are resolved. No article text, table, figure, or dataset was copied.

decision.reason: The abstract supports a valuable but historical, site- and size-dependent diet finding. The full text was not reviewed and item-level license applicability is unresolved, so no public diet card is approved.

nextAction: Verify the 2018 article's item-level license and review the publisher full text, especially the complete prey list and length-class definitions, before considering a concise, attributed Laguna de Bay diet card. Keep diet evidence separate from bait effectiveness, catchability, presence, safety, and legal status.

sources.supports: Official publisher citation, abstract, study period, reported sample, sites, leading prey, and size/site differences.
Current journal-wide statement that AFS articles use CC BY-NC 4.0; the article-level applicability to this 2018 item remains unverified.
